 Search BIR Moves Metro Manila Tax Deadlines to November 19, 2026: Who Is Covered
 Atty. Yasser R. Aureada, CPA 4 days ago 3 min read The BIR moved to November 19, 2026 the deadline for filing returns and paying taxes whose statutory due dates fall on November 16 to 18, 2026. The change is in a Tax Advisory issued on November 10, 2026. It covers taxpayers under the BIR offices in the National Capital Region (NCR) that the advisory lists. The three days were declared special (non-working) days in the NCR by Proclamation No. 1447, September 17, 2026, in connection with the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits. 
 Read the full text: Tax Advisory, November 10, 2026 (Bureau of Internal Revenue) 
 What did the BIR change? 
 The advisory states that the deadline for the filing of returns and payment of taxes "with statutory due dates falling during the said period" shall be moved to November 19, 2026. The period referred to is November 16 to 18, 2026. 
 So a return or a tax payment that the law makes due on November 16, 17 or 18, 2026 may be filed and paid until Thursday, November 19, 2026, if the taxpayer is covered. 
 Why were the deadlines moved? 
 Proclamation No. 1447, dated September 17, 2026, declared November 16 to 18, 2026 as special (non-working) days in the National Capital Region. The advisory states that this was in connection with the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits. The BIR advisory was issued pursuant to that proclamation. 
 Who is covered by the November 19 deadline? 
 Only taxpayers within the jurisdiction of the BIR offices under the NCR that are listed in the advisory. The list is made up of Revenue District Offices and Large Taxpayer offices in Metro Manila. 
 Check the list in the advisory itself. The full text is linked above. Look for the number of your own Revenue District Office. 
 How do you know your Revenue District Office? 
 As a practical step, look at your BIR Certificate of Registration. It shows the Revenue District Office where the business is registered. A business with branches should check the office of each branch, because the advisory goes by the office that has jurisdiction. 
 Which deadlines are moved? 
 The advisory speaks of two things only: the filing of returns and the payment of taxes. It applies to those with statutory due dates on November 16 to 18, 2026. 
 The advisory does not mention other filings or submissions. Do not assume that a deadline not named in the advisory was also moved. Other regular due dates are in the BIR, SEC and BSP compliance calendar . 
 Are taxpayers outside Metro Manila covered? 
 The advisory lists only offices under the NCR. It does not move any deadline for taxpayers registered with BIR offices that are not on its list. 
 What happens if a covered taxpayer misses November 19? 
 The advisory tells taxpayers to file their returns and pay the taxes within the adjusted deadline to avoid applicable penalties. The consequences of late filing are explained in the guide on what happens if you miss a BIR deadline . 
 What should a business do this week? 
 These are practical steps, not requirements of the advisory: 
 Confirm that your Revenue District Office is on the list. 
 List the returns and payments of your business that fall due on November 16 to 18, 2026. 
 File and pay before November 19 if you can. In practice, last-day filing leaves no room for a system or bank problem. 
 Keep a copy of the advisory with your filing records. 
 Start on the year-end work early. See the year-end tax compliance checklist . 
 Frequently asked questions 
 Is November 19, 2026 the new deadline for all taxpayers in the Philippines? 
 No. 
 The advisory covers only taxpayers within the jurisdiction of the NCR offices it lists. 
 Does the advisory extend the period to file a protest with the BIR? 
 The advisory mentions only the filing of returns and the payment of taxes. Protest periods are discussed in the post on BIR RMC No. 116-2026 . 
 Which due dates are covered? 
 Statutory due dates that fall on November 16, 17 or 18, 2026. 
 Sources 
 Tax Advisory, November 10, 2026 (Bureau of Internal Revenue) 
 Proclamation No. 1447, September 17, 2026 (Office of the President)
